name: Roasted Carrots and Parsnips
description: A simple roasted vegetable dish featuring carrots, parsnips, and onions with a maple syrup and mustard glaze.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb parsnips, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place parsnips, carrots, onions, oil, and thyme in a prepared baking dish; toss until vegetables are well coated with oil.
Roast in the oven for 30 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine maple syrup and mustard.
Pour the maple syrup mixture over the vegetables and toss to coat.
Roast for another 20 to 25 minutes or until vegetables are tender and golden, stirring once.

keywords: roasted carrots, roasted parsnips, maple syrup glaze

_similar.name: Sliced Baked Potatoes
_similar.description: A simple yet elegant baked potato dish featuring thinly sliced potatoes topped with melted cheddar and Parmesan cheese, and fresh herbs.
recipeIngredient: 2-3 Tbsp fresh chopped herbs (such as parsley, chives, thyme, or sage)

recipeInstructions.text: Scrub and rinse the potatoes.
Cut the potatoes crosswise into thin slices, but not all the way through. Use the handle of a wooden spoon on either side of the potato to guide the knife.
Place the potatoes on a baking sheet and fan them slightly.
Drizzle the potatoes with melted butter and sprinkle with fresh herbs.
Bake at 425°F for about 50 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheddar and Parmesan cheese and return to the oven until the cheese is lightly browned and the potatoes are soft inside.

_similar.keywords: baked potatoes, sliced potatoes, cheesy potatoes, herbed potatoes

_similar.name: Roasted Chestnuts
_similar.description: Tender and flavorful roasted chestnuts seasoned with butter, salt, and cinnamon.

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Cut a ½-inch crisscross on the flat side of each chestnut, ensuring the cut goes through the nut to prevent explosion during baking.
Place the scored chestnuts in a shallow baking pan and bake for 25 to 30 minutes.
Allow the chestnuts to cool, then peel off the shells.
In a skillet, melt the butter over high heat and sauté the peeled chestnuts until well coated.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and roast until the chestnuts are golden on top.
Sprinkle with salt and cinnamon to taste before serving.

_similar.keywords: roasted chestnuts, savory snack, holiday appetizer

_similar.name: Meat and Potato Casserole
_similar.description: A hearty casserole with ground beef, sliced potatoes, and corn, topped with a savory gravy.

recipeInstructions.text: Brown the ground beef with onion and garlic. Season with salt and pepper.
Layer sliced potatoes in an 8L casserole dish.
Mix the gravy mix with 1 cup water and pour over the potatoes. Add remaining water.
Top with corn and the browned meat mixture.
Cover and cook at 350°F for 50 minutes.

_similar.keywords: meat casserole, potato and corn dish, gravy topping

_similar.name: Turkey or Chicken Pies
_similar.description: Individual or large pies filled with turkey or chicken, vegetables, and a creamy sauce, topped with a homemade pastry crust or biscuits.
_similar.recipeYield: Multiple individual pies or 1 large pie

recipeInstructions.text: Melt margarine with salt and pepper over low heat. Add flour and gradually add broth, cooking until smooth.
Sauté chopped onion and celery until tender.
Boil carrots until thoroughly cooked.
Mix cooked carrots with peas and the sauce made earlier.
For the pastry, mix flour, salt, and baking powder with butter. Add milk to form a dough.
Fill small pans or a large pie plate with the turkey or chicken mixture and top with pastry crust or biscuits.
Bake until the crust is golden brown.

_similar.keywords: turkey pie, chicken pie, savory pastry, comfort food

_similar.name: Cabbage Rolls
_similar.description: Traditional cabbage rolls filled with a savory mixture of ground pork, beef, and rice, simmered in tomato juice.

recipeInstructions.text: Boil the cabbage head for 10 minutes to soften the leaves. Drain and let cool.
Chop the onion and fry in lard for 10 minutes until softened.
Mix the cooked onion and lard with ground pork, ground beef, rice, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Peel off cabbage leaves and cut out the thick stem. Place about 1 tablespoon of the meat mixture in the center of each leaf, fold the sides, and roll into a neat package.
Line the bottom of a large pot with a layer of cabbage leaves to prevent burning.
Arrange the cabbage rolls seam-side down in the pot, layering them as needed.
Pour the tomato juice over the cabbage rolls, ensuring they are mostly covered.
Bring the tomato juice to a simmer, then reduce heat and let cook for the entire afternoon (approximately 3 hours).

_similar.keywords: cabbage rolls, stuffed cabbage, ground meat, comfort food
